newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Aug 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Aug 4.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Monday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal.
* Corporate profits grew 5.0 percent in the second quarter as more companies pursued growth plans both at home and abroad.
* The U.S. economy added a stronger-than-expected 316,000 new jobs in July and the jobless rate fell to 4.8 percent.
* Stock and bond prices tumbled Friday amid renewed inflation fears, although stocks recouped much of their losses by the end of trading.
* General Motors Corp said its U.S. sales of cars and light trucks rose 6.5 percent in July, while Chrysler Corp said its sales were off 9.0 percent.
* Barney's said it accepted a bid from Dickson Concepts to buy control of the retailer.
* Apple Computer will not withhold its latest available technology from cloners of its computers, although seems reluctant to share future advances.
* Wheeling-Pittsburgh reached an agreement with its steelworkers to end the longest major steel-industry strike this century.
* Bethlehem Steel said it was selling two unprofitable units and that talks to sell a third had broken off.
* United Parcel Service faced a midnight strike deadline as the Teamsters walked out of federally mediated contract talks last night.
* General Electric shuffled its top executives, apparently to groom contenders to suceed Chairman Jack Welch.
* Ritz-Carlton Hotel removed its name from four properties it managed.
* PacifiCorp's $5.8 billion plan to buy Britain's Energy Group hit a potentially serious roadblock after the government decided to conduct a regulatory inquiry.
* Boeing will set up headquarters for its military-aircraft lines at the former McDonnell's St. Louis home.
* Air Canada signed a letter of intent to buy eight Airbus wide-body jets.
* Parametric Technology was ordered to pay an ex-executive $1.6 million after a jury found the company fired him because he was about to exercise his stock options.
* Lee and Ed Bass are expected to sell their Southern California water rights to U.S. Filter for more than $250 million in stock.
* Marvin Davis agreed to form a joint venture with ITT Corp $339.5 million, after $467.7 million of charges.
* Grand Union will name J. Wayne Harris as chairman and chief executive.
* CellPro said the NIH declined to intervene on its behalf in a patent dispute with Baxter Healthcare and Becton Dickinson.
* Falconbridge was hit by a strike that shut down almost half of its nickel production.
* Some Wall Streeters think ITT Corp's stock is overvalued, trading now at a rich ten times cash flow estimates for 1997 made by Salomon Brothers.
* While few on Wall Street expect the Federal Reserve Board to boost rates in the near future, bonds' sharp price gains in recent weeks seem to be over for now.
((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610))
